column1: # Beliefs: the premises the whole argument starts from. They are normative: lines the author
# draws, not facts a quote can prove, so they never pass Descartes and wait on circle 4 (author sign-off).
# Every card is read against them; a reader who rejects one can see exactly which conclusions it carries.
# source: where the author said it. state: stated (said, not yet signed) | signed (circle 4).

column2: To be any kind of company, you ought to be in effective control of your surrounding environment.
Governance exists so that systems can survive individuals.
The question that matters, of anyone: am I in control of the systems I use to make decisions, operate, and balance competing priorities?
A public benefit corporation is supposed to be a thing built, at its core, to do what it says.
Impact is not a single currency: a forecast benefit does not offset a present harm unless a governance forces the reconciliation.
